results.title: OpenRouter Reviews 2026: Honest Verdict From Real Users
results.content:
Verified founder OpenRouter reviews praise multi-model access, fast switching, and a single endpoint. Developers value a single key, a single account, and a single interface across hundreds of models. This reduces integration work during early development, especially when teams compare model quality, latency, and pricing across providers.

### What are the most common complaints in OpenRouter customer reviews on Trustpilot?

The most common complaints in OpenRouter customer reviews concern support delays, account security handling, and agentic workloads that create unexpected costs. Several users describe slow responses from support channels. Others mention rate-limit friction and cost spikes during agent loops where no hard budget stopped the session early. [...] Favorable OpenRouter reviews cluster around Product Hunt. Most positive comments come from founders and builders who used OpenRouter during product development. Read in volume, the praise centers on lower integration effort, fast model switching, and easier provider experimentation.

### Unified Multi-Model Access Without Managing Multiple API Keys

The most common positive theme is reduced engineering overhead. Teams that once managed separate keys, SDKs, provider accounts, and invoices describe OpenRouter as collapsing that work into one layer. A single API helps smaller teams move faster. [...] ## What OpenRouter User Reviews Flag as Limitations

The critical reviews come from a different source and a different kind of user. On Trustpilot, OpenRouter holds a TrustScore of 1.7 out of 5 across 41 reviews as of May 2026, with 79% of them rated one star. The complaints are not scattered. They concentrate on a few specific failures that matter most at the production scale.

### Customer Support Does Not Respond Reliably

The dominant complaint is poor responsiveness from support. Reviewers describe filing requests and waiting weeks for replies. Several mention Discord as the primary support channel, rather than a structured ticketing process suited to urgent production issues.

results.title: OpenRouter MCP Server - OpenRouter
results.content:
## ​ How it works

1. Discovery & auth. An unauthenticated request returns a `401` that points your client to OpenRouter’s OAuth authorization server. The client registers, you approve the consent page, and a token is issued via PKCE.
2. Dedicated key. The issued token is a standard OpenRouter API key labeled `OpenRouter MCP:` , minted with a 7-day expiry and a `$10` default spend limit so you can find and revoke it from your dashboard.
3. Live data, no local state. Tools proxy the public OpenRouter API with your key. Nothing is installed locally, and no source code is sent anywhere unless you call `send-message`, `generate-image`, or `send-feedback`.

## ​ Troubleshooting [...] Not all clients pop up the auth automatically; some need a one-time login step after you add the server. When you trigger it, an OpenRouter consent page opens in your browser where you approve a dedicated key just for this connection, separate from your other keys. The key expires after 7 days and starts with a `$10` spend cap (editable on the approval screen). You can disconnect anytime.

## ​ What you can do

The MCP exposes these tools. Most are read-only lookups against live OpenRouter data. Two exceptions exist. `send-message` and `generate-image` make billable inference calls, and `send-feedback` writes feedback on one of your own generations. [...] ## ​ Troubleshooting

 Tool calls fail with an auth error. Re-run the authenticate step for your client. The key may have expired (7-day lifetime) or been disconnected.
 The login didn’t pop automatically. Some clients require a manual trigger. Use the per-client step above.

Responses are generated using AI and may contain mistakes.

| Server exits immediately / `OPENROUTER_API_KEY is required` | Missing or empty API key | Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in client `env` or shell — get one at openrouter.ai/keys |
| `_meta.code: INVALID_CREDENTIALS` or HTTP 401 | Bad or revoked key | Regenerate at openrouter.ai/keys; restart the MCP client |
| `_meta.code: MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | Typo or retired model ID | Run `search_models` or `validate_model`; check openrouter.ai/models |
| HTTP 402 / insufficient credits | Paid model or generation on zero balance | Add credits at openrouter.ai/credits or use a `:free` model |
| `_meta.code: UPSTREAM_HTTP` with 429 | Rate limit | Wait for `_meta.retry_after_seconds` if present; reduce concurrency | [...] npm global
